constraints: This is a non-batch, zero-experiment, zero-implementation pre-compute gate check. Do NOT implement or time any p-adic arithmetic, do NOT write or run any code, and do NOT create B71, BATCH, EV, DEC, CORR, experiment, or implementation records. This task may write exactly the four declared artifacts and nothing else.

Do NOT change ECDLP-IDEA-436's own 'Status and claim labels' block or any other field of ideas/ECDLP-IDEA-436_local_torsion_coordinate_valuation_profile_hypothesis.md itself -- that record is frozen; this task's own recommendation goes in the new gate memo, and any status change to the idea record itself is a separate, later Coordinator action.

The GGM-simulability question, precisely: is the map from (E, S, j, k, r) -> inv_{j,r}(k) computable using only generic group operations (group law, equality test, random group-element sampling) and NO coordinate-level or p-adic-arithmetic access beyond what a generic group oracle exposes? A p-adic valuation of a coordinate DIFFERENCE is not obviously a generic-group-computable quantity (coordinates and valuations are extra structure a generic group oracle does not expose), so do not assume simulability or non-simulability without a genuine argument -- this is exactly the open question ECDLP-IDEA-436 flags as needing to be checked first, and it may resolve either way.

If concluding SIMULABLE: name the exact simulation procedure (what generic-group operations compute inv_{j,r}(k), and with what overhead), and confirm it fits the mechanism of KN-FIND-002's or KN-FIND-b7e091's existing closure (jet/endomorphism/incidence oracle simulability) or explain precisely how it differs while still being simulable.

If concluding NOT SIMULABLE: name the exact operation in the profile's computation (e.g. reading a specific p-adic coordinate digit, or a valuation comparison) that a generic group oracle cannot provide, and explain why no combination of group operations and equality tests can reproduce it. Do not conflate 'not simulable' with 'therefore useful' -- ECDLP-IDEA-436's own record states the lift is information-theoretically empty (KN-TECH-73630e), so non-simulability alone does not imply the family is efficiently invertible or cost-competitive; that is separately gated by the idea's own precision-growth obstruction, which this task does not need to resolve.

If the finding is ambiguous or depends on an unstated formalization choice (e.g. exactly what 'generic group oracle' access to E(Q_p) vs E(F_p) means, or whether the oracle is defined over the lift or the reduction), state this explicitly as an open formalization question rather than picking a convenient reading -- this is exactly the kind of premature-closure failure mode this program's inventor protocol treats as symmetric with overclaiming.

Controls before belief: apply a proves-too-much check -- if your simulability argument, run on the ALREADY-CLOSED jet or endomorphism oracle (KN-FIND-002), gives a different (wrong) verdict than what KN-FIND-002 already established, your argument is broken and must be revised before being trusted on the new valuation-profile oracle.

Citation provenance is mandatory: recalled | retrieved | kb | internal on every source. KN-FIND-002, KN-FIND-b7e091, KN-TECH-73630e, KN-TECH-06bb4e are internal/kb entries in this corpus and must be opened and quoted accurately, not paraphrased from memory.

YAML/Markdown hygiene: for the YAML deliverables, no plain scalar may contain an embedded, unescaped double-quote or a colon-followed-by-space -- wrap the ENTIRE scalar in single quotes if either is needed. No duplicated top-level keys at any nesting level, no bare mapping key inside a block sequence without a leading '-'. This defect class has broken artifacts in multiple prior rounds on this goal; check every free-text field and every list line by line before finishing.
